specification:
Terminal window title setting

## Goals
- Let an application request a change of the terminal window title through the Console, using the same control path as the existing cursor and screen controls.
- Make the request effective on ANSI-capable terminals by emitting the OSC 0 title sequence, and on legacy Windows consoles by dispatching the title to the existing legacy Windows renderer, which calls the wrapper's set-title method.
- Report through a boolean result whether the title control was written to the output buffer.

## Scope
- In scope: one new control type; one classmethod on the Control class that builds the title control; one Console method; one new branch in the legacy Windows renderer; one CHANGELOG entry; the tests listed under Test requirements.
- Out of scope: reading the title; resetting or restoring a previous title; sanitizing or transforming title text; changing existing control types, their values, or their output; new configuration options; changes to the Windows console wrapper class.
- Contributor checklists, pull-request type selections, review-process notes, and mentions of individuals are not part of the feature and must not appear in the specification or in code comments.

## Assumptions
- Legacy Windows detection, and the standard-stream check that selects the legacy render path at buffer flush, already exist and are correct. This feature does not change them.
- The legacy Windows wrapper already provides a method that sets the console title. It is reused, not reimplemented.
- Other software (the shell, a prompt, the terminal itself) may overwrite the title at any time, so the feature does not guarantee that a title persists.

## Terminology
- Terminal: a Console for which the terminal check is true. This is the same check that show_cursor uses.
- Legacy Windows console: a Console whose legacy-windows flag is set, meaning Windows without virtual-terminal (VT) escape processing.
- Standard stream: an output stream that the legacy render path can address directly. The render path checks this at buffer flush.
- Title control: a control code whose type is the new SET_WINDOW_TITLE member and whose parameter is the title text.
- Title sequence: the escape sequence consisting of the ESC character, a right bracket, the digit zero, a semicolon, the title text, and the BEL character (code 0x07). This is OSC 0 with a BEL terminator.

## Workflows
1. The application asks the Console to set the window title to a text value.
2. The Console method checks only whether the console is a terminal. It must not check the legacy-windows flag. This matches show_cursor, not set_alt_screen.
   - If the console is not a terminal: buffer nothing and return false.
   - If it is a terminal: build a title control from the text, add its segment to the buffer through the existing control path, and return true.
3. At buffer flush, if the console is a legacy Windows console and the output file is a standard stream, the buffer goes to the legacy renderer. For each title control, in buffer order, the renderer calls the wrapper's set-title method once, passing the title text.
4. On all other render paths, the title segment carries the title sequence as its text and follows the ordinary render rules. Control segments are dropped when the output is not a terminal.
5. A true result means the sequence was written to the buffer. It does not confirm that the title changed.

## Data model
- Control type enumeration: add exactly one member, named SET_WINDOW_TITLE, with the next integer after the highest existing value. Do not renumber existing members.
- Control code: a control code is a tuple whose first item is the control type and whose remaining items are parameters. The title control code is a two-item form: the control type followed by the title text.
- The declared union of allowed control code shapes must also admit the two-item form of a control type followed by text. Existing shapes stay admitted. The union must type-check under the repository's mypy configuration.
- The title text is stored in the control code exactly as given. No transformation is applied at the data level.

## API contracts
- Console method: name set_window_title; one positional parameter named title that is text; returns a boolean. Returns true when the title control was written to the buffer. Returns false when the console is not a terminal, and in that case nothing is written. It must never return nothing, and it must not raise for non-terminal consoles.
- Control classmethod: name title; one text parameter named title; returns a Control. The Control's segment text is the title sequence, its style is none, and its control list holds exactly one title control code.
- Construction rule: a title control must be passed to the Control constructor as a single two-item argument (control type and title text). Do not pass the control type and the title as two separate positional arguments. The constructor treats each positional argument as either a bare control type or a control code, so a bare text argument is misread as a sequence of codes and construction fails at runtime.
- Format entry: for the title control type, the text formatter takes the title text and returns the title sequence.
- Legacy renderer contract: for a title control code, read the title text from the second item of the code and call the wrapper's set-title method with that text as its only argument.

## Module architecture
- Segment module: holds the enum member and the control code union.
- Control module: holds the formatting table entry and the Control classmethod. Escape bytes live only here.
- Console module: holds the set_window_title method, placed beside show_cursor and set_alt_screen. It delegates to the control path and contains no Windows API calls and no legacy checks.
- Windows renderer module: holds the one new branch in the legacy render dispatch, which is where Windows-side handling of control types belongs.
- Win32 console wrapper: unchanged. Its existing set-title method is reused.
- Dependency direction: Console depends on Control, which depends on Segment. The renderer depends on the wrapper and Segment. No module may import upward or create a cycle.

## Implementation constraints
- Add the renderer branch to the existing if/elif chain over control types, placed with the other control types, and follow the pattern of the parameterized controls: interpret the code in its two-item form, then read the parameter.
- Gate the Console method only on the terminal check. Do not gate it on the legacy-windows flag, and do not add any console-level guard that returns false for legacy consoles. The legacy path is handled by the renderer.
- Register the new control type in all three places: the formatting table, the enum and union, and the legacy renderer dispatch. Omitting any one of them is a defect.
- Do not change the values or output format of any existing control type.
- Do not add Windows-specific logic to the Console or Control modules.

## Dependencies
- Introduce no new third-party or standard-library imports. The renderer already imports the typing names and control types it needs; reuse them.
- Reuse the wrapper's existing set-title method. It asserts that the title is shorter than 255 characters. Inherit that behavior; do not duplicate it.

## Naming
- Enum member: SET_WINDOW_TITLE.
- Console method: set_window_title, with a parameter named title.
- Control classmethod: title, matching the short classmethod style of bell, home, and alt_screen.
- Test names follow the existing test-file naming pattern (see Test requirements).

## Validation
- Do not add type checks or content checks to the Console method or to the Control classmethod. The title is not trimmed, checked, or escaped beyond what is described above.

## Error handling
- Writing to a non-terminal console is not an error. Return false.
- Do not catch or convert exceptions raised by the wrapper's set-title method. Its length assertion propagates on legacy consoles.
- Do not introduce new exception types.

## Logging
- Add no logging.

## Documentation
- The Console method docstring follows the repository's Google style, with a summary line and Args and Returns sections. It must state these warnings: Rich provides no way to reset the title to its previous value, so the title persists after the application exits; some shells reset titles before and after each command and most do not; some terminals need configuration changes or do not support titles; other software may overwrite the title; and a true result means only that the control was written, not that the title changed.
- The Control classmethod docstring has a summary line and an Args entry for title.
- CHANGELOG: add one bullet under the Unreleased section, under an Added heading. Create that heading above the Fixed heading if it is missing. The bullet describes the ability to change the terminal window title, links to pull request 2200, and follows the existing bullet format.

## Security
- The title text is written into the escape sequence unmodified, as in the reference implementation. Do not add stripping or escaping unless it leaves ordinary titles byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Reliability
- When the console is not a terminal, including when recording is enabled or output is redirected, no title sequence may enter the buffer. Escape text must never reach pipes, recordings, or exported text through this method.
- On legacy consoles, the title call must occur only on the standard-stream render path. Redirected legacy output must not reach the Windows title call.

## Maintainability
- Use the existing control-type extension mechanism: the enum, the formatting table, the union, and the legacy renderer dispatch. Do not create a parallel path or a legacy-only branch in the Console.

## Compatibility
- Existing control types, their escape output, and the legacy renderer behavior for other control types are unchanged.
- Widening the control code union is additive.
- Code that does not call the new method or classmethod is unaffected.

## Behavioral acceptance criteria
- On a terminal that is not a legacy console, set_window_title with the text "hello" writes exactly the title sequence for "hello" and returns true.
- On a console that is not a terminal (including recording and redirected output), set_window_title writes nothing and returns false.
- Control.title with "hello" yields a segment whose text is the title sequence, with no style, and whose control list holds exactly one title control code containing the title control type and "hello".
- Constructing the title control does not raise.
- The legacy renderer, given a segment carrying one title control code with "hello", calls the wrapper's set-title method exactly once with "hello" and makes no other terminal call for that code.
- On a legacy Windows console writing to a standard stream, set_window_title results in the set-title call when the buffer is rendered.

## Test requirements
- Console test (all platforms): create a console with forced terminal output and an empty environment. If the console is a legacy Windows console, return without asserting. Otherwise capture the output of set_window_title with the text "hello", and assert that the captured text equals the title sequence for "hello" and that the return value is true.
- Control test: assert that Control.title with "hello" produces a segment equal to the title sequence text, no style, and a control list containing exactly the title control type paired with "hello".
- Renderer test (Windows only; skip on other platforms): use a mocked wrapper, render a buffer containing one segment whose control list holds a title control with the text "Hello, world!", and assert that the set-title method was called exactly once with that text.
- Place the tests in the existing test modules for the Console, Control, and Windows renderer, following their current patterns.
- No other test changes are required by this feature.

edits.change: Replace the pull-request description opening with explicit goals: request a window title change through the Console; make it effective on ANSI terminals (OSC 0) and on legacy Windows consoles through the legacy renderer and the existing wrapper set-title method; report success as a boolean.
edits.hypothesis: The current draft is a PR description with no behavioral goals. It never states the legacy Windows requirement, which is the basis of requirement_intent failures in runs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9.

edits.change: Define in-scope items (one control type, one Control classmethod, one Console method, one legacy renderer branch, CHANGELOG entry, tests) and out-of-scope items (reading or resetting titles, sanitizing titles, changing existing control types, wrapper changes).
edits.hypothesis: Without an explicit scope, agents added unrequested sanitization and extra logic (run 0) and touched unrelated areas; a bounded scope keeps the patch to the reference footprint, supporting file_location and architectural_fit.

edits.change: Remove the contributor checklist, pull-request type selections, the bare contributor mention, and review-process notes from the specification text.
edits.hypothesis: These are not feature requirements. The bare mention would notify an individual, and the checklist could be read as requirements, which creates ambiguity under convention_fit.

edits.change: Define terminal (terminal check, same as show_cursor), legacy Windows console (legacy-windows flag), standard stream (checked at flush), title control, and title sequence (OSC 0 with BEL terminator).
edits.hypothesis: Undefined terms let agents conflate the terminal check with the legacy check. Runs 0, 3, 8 and 9 gated on the legacy flag because they treated the alt-screen gating as the model; defining the terms addresses extension_point_adherence and requirement_intent.

edits.change: State that legacy detection and the standard-stream check already exist and are unchanged, that the wrapper's set-title method is reused, and that other software may overwrite the title.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 0 and 3 implied that legacy handling had to be rebuilt in the Console. Stating that the wrapper's existing method is reused directs the change to the renderer, addressing extension_point_adherence.

edits.change: Specify the Console flow: check only the terminal check (not the legacy flag); when false, buffer nothing and return false; when true, build the title control, add it through the existing control path, and return true. Explicitly reference show_cursor as the pattern rather than set_alt_screen.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 1, 2, 4, 7 and 9 returned nothing from set_window_title, and runs 0, 3 and 8 added a legacy-flag gate that produced a silent no-op. This step fixes the return contract and removes the gate, addressing api_contract, extension_point_adherence and convention_fit.

edits.change: Specify the legacy flush path: when the console is a legacy Windows console writing to a standard stream, each title control in buffer order results in exactly one set-title call with the title text. On other paths, the title segment follows ordinary render rules.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 failed extension_registration because the renderer had no title branch, so the title was silently dropped on legacy consoles. Specifying this flow addresses that failure and the requirement_intent gap on legacy consoles.

edits.change: Add a new enum member named SET_WINDOW_TITLE after the highest existing value; state that the control code's two-item form (type plus text) must be admitted by the declared union, while existing shapes remain; state that the text is stored unmodified.
edits.hypothesis: Run 6 flagged that the union was not widened so the declared constructor type rejects the title tuple, and run 7 flagged the unregistered shape. Specifying the union widening addresses extension_registration and api_contract.

edits.change: Specify the Console method contract: name set_window_title, one text parameter named title, returns a boolean that is true if the control was written and false for a non-terminal console (nothing written). It must never return nothing and must not raise for non-terminal consoles.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 1, 2, 4, 7 and 9 failed api_contract because the method returned nothing. The reference returns a boolean, and a boolean contract lets callers detect the no-op case.

edits.change: Add the construction rule: pass the title control to the Control constructor as a single two-item argument (type plus text); do not pass the type and title as separate positional arguments, because the constructor misreads a bare text argument as control codes.
edits.hypothesis: Run 8 failed api_contract and requirement_intent with a runtime failure: the generated Control classmethod called the constructor with the type and the title as two positional arguments (verified in run-08 control.py). The constructor iterates each positional argument, so the title text was misread as codes and construction failed. This rule addresses that failing operation.

edits.change: Specify the Control classmethod (name title, one text parameter, returns a Control whose segment text is the title sequence, no style, and one title control code), the format entry for the title sequence, and the legacy renderer contract (read the title from the second item and call the wrapper's set-title method with it).
edits.hypothesis: These contracts make the three registration points explicit, addressing extension_registration and the requirement that the Control classmethod return contract matches the reference.

edits.change: Assign responsibilities: enum and union in the segment module; formatting entry and classmethod in the control module; Console method beside show_cursor and set_alt_screen with no Windows calls; the legacy renderer branch in the Windows renderer module; the wrapper unchanged; dependency direction Console to Control to Segment.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 4 and 7 failed file_location because the Windows-side handling was not in the renderer module. Stating the layer assignment addresses file_location and architectural_fit.

edits.change: Require the renderer branch in the existing control-type chain; forbid gating the Console method on the legacy flag or adding a console-level legacy guard; require registration in all three places (format table, enum and union, renderer); forbid changes to existing control values and forbid Windows-specific logic in Console or Control.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 0, 3, 6, 8 and 9 failed extension_point_adherence by gating legacy consoles off instead of extending the renderer. Runs 0 through 9 failed extension_registration for the missing renderer branch. These constraints address both.

edits.change: State that no new imports or third-party or standard-library dependencies are needed, that the renderer's existing typing and control-type imports are reused, and that the wrapper's existing set-title method (with its 255-character assertion) is inherited.
edits.hypothesis: This preserves the approved_dependencies requirement and prevents a new wrapper or import being added to the Console path. The clarification supports dependency_direction and approved_dependencies.

edits.change: Specify the names: enum member SET_WINDOW_TITLE; Console method set_window_title with parameter title; Control classmethod title, matching the bell, home, and alt_screen style.
edits.hypothesis: Run 9 failed convention_fit, and run 7 flagged an inconsistent alias; naming the members in the same style as siblings addresses convention_fit and api_contract naming.

edits.change: State that no type or content validation is added to the Console method or the Control classmethod, and that the title is not trimmed or checked.
edits.hypothesis: This preserves the reference behavior, which performs no validation, and prevents added checks that change the contract. It supports convention_fit and api_contract.

edits.change: State that writing to a non-terminal console is not an error and returns false; that exceptions from the wrapper's set-title method, including its length assertion, must propagate; and that no new exception types are introduced.
edits.hypothesis: Clarifies the non-terminal path so it returns the boolean result rather than raising, supporting api_contract, and prevents exception wrapping that the reference does not use.

edits.change: State that no logging is added.
edits.hypothesis: Explicitly bounds the change so that no logging is added. This preserves the repository convention for the legacy render path and supports convention_fit.

edits.change: Require the Console docstring in Google style with Args and Returns, carrying the warnings about no reset, shell and terminal variation, configuration needs, overwriting by other software, and the meaning of true as written-not-changed. Require the Control docstring summary and title arg. Require a CHANGELOG bullet under an Added heading in Unreleased, with a link to pull request 2200 in the existing bullet style.
edits.hypothesis: Run 1 and run 9 depended on the documented return meaning, and run 0 flagged the CHANGELOG bullet missing its PR link. These requirements address api_contract documentation and convention_fit.

edits.change: State that the title text is embedded unmodified, matching the reference, and that stripping or escaping may be added only if ordinary titles remain byte-for-byte identical.
edits.hypothesis: The current draft is silent on title content. This removes ambiguity about the reference behavior; runs 0 and 7 added stripping that was judged acceptable, and this sets the boundary without forbidding it outright.

edits.change: Require that no title sequence enters the buffer when the console is not a terminal, including recording and redirected output, and that redirected legacy output never reaches the Windows title call.
edits.hypothesis: Run 9 raised escape leakage into recorded or exported text, and run 2 raised the redirected legacy path. The terminal-check gate in the reference prevents both, so requiring it addresses requirement_intent.

edits.change: Require that the feature use the existing control-type mechanism (enum, formatting table, union, legacy renderer dispatch) and forbid a parallel path or a legacy-only Console branch.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 0, 3, 6, 8 and 9 each built a separate legacy no-op path. Requiring the existing mechanism addresses extension_point_adherence and maintainability of the dispatch chain.

edits.change: State that existing control types, their escape output, and legacy renderer behavior for other types are unchanged; the union widening is additive; code that does not use the new method is unaffected.
edits.hypothesis: This protects the currently satisfied behavior so that fixes do not change existing controls, and it keeps the union change additive, as the reference is.

edits.change: List the acceptance criteria: terminal non-legacy writes the exact title sequence and returns true; non-terminal (including recording and redirected) writes nothing and returns false; Control.title yields the expected segment and single title code; construction does not raise; the legacy renderer calls set-title exactly once with the text; a legacy console writing to a standard stream sets the title at render time.
edits.hypothesis: These criteria make each failed behavior testable: the None return, the TypeError at construction, the missing legacy dispatch, and the leakage to non-terminal output. They address api_contract, requirement_intent and extension_registration.

edits.change: Require a Console test (forced terminal, empty environment, skip assertions on legacy consoles, assert exact sequence and true return), a Control test (segment text, no style, single title pair), and a Windows-only renderer test (mocked wrapper, set-title called once with the text). Place tests in the existing test modules.
edits.hypothesis: Runs 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 flagged missing tests for the Console method, the renderer branch, and the control. Requiring these tests addresses convention_fit and the test-coverage gap, and the renderer test catches the missing-dispatch failure.
